claims: Primal-Attention embeds unsupervised KSVD optimization by adding a regularization term to the training loss, avoiding any extra decomposition operations [2][5].
This regularization loss promotes a low-rank property of the attention kernel and satisfies the KSVD stationarity conditions when its objective reaches zero [3][1].
Thus, the KSVD optimization is efficiently integrated into training through a simple auxiliary loss rather than explicit kernel-matrix computation [4].
FSLoRA keeps the full-rank LoRA modules on the central server while clients only update selected submatrices of these modules according to sketching ratios [1][2].
By tuning the sketching ratios, which set the rank of each client’s submatrix, the framework lets each client match its own communication bandwidth and computational capacity [2][3].
Clients with more resources can choose larger submatrix ranks, leading to faster convergence, whereas limited clients use smaller ranks to reduce overhead [4].
